svg.title: Where defects in cytotoxic killing cause familial HLH (single colour)
svg.desc: An NK cell or cytotoxic T cell kills an EBV-infected cell: its granules form and move to the synapse, dock and fuse there, and release perforin, which makes pores in the target. Inherited defects stop each step: LYST and AP3B1 in forming and moving the granules; RAB27A, UNC13D, STX11 and STXBP2 in docking and fusion; and PRF1, perforin itself. When killing fails, the killer cells stay activated, interferon gamma activates macrophages, and macrophages engulf blood cells: haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
